classification.classification_note: The observed memory error is an out-of-bounds read caused by confusing the internal dense X86 `InstrUID` domain with the sparse public `insns[]` mapping-table index domain.

bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.report.comments[0].content / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / local Capstone history
bug_description.normalized: In the exact staged Capstone checkout (`6bdc66c0`), the 7-byte witness `00 62 f1 fd 20 15 20` first selects `platforms[0] = { CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32 }`, then reaches `readPrefixes()` as the X86 stream `62 f1 fd 20 15 20`. `readPrefixes()` accepts `62 f1 fd 20` as EVEX even in 32-bit mode and persists those four attacker bytes in `vectorExtensionType` and `vectorExtensionPrefix[0..3]`. `readOpcode()` uses the EVEX `mm` field from `0xf1` to pick the 0F map and consumes opcode `0x15`; `getID()` then derives an EVEX attribute mask from the same stored prefix bytes, with `ppFromEVEX3of4(0xfd) == VEX_PREFIX_66`, `wFromEVEX3of4(0xfd) == 1`, and `lFromEVEX4of4(0x20) == 1`. During the first `getIDWithAttrMask()` call, `readModRM()` consumes the next byte `0x20` into `insn->modRM`. Because the instruction is still in `MODE_32BIT` and the EVEX W bit is set, `getID()` performs a second `getIDWithAttrMask(..., attrMask | ATTR_REXW)` lookup using the same opcode `0x15` and stored ModR/M byte `0x20`. Vulnerable `is64Bit()` then uses that internal lookup result directly as `insns[id]`, even though `insns[]` is a 14,219-element public mapping table rather than a dense internal UID array. From the saved ASan report's 83,684-byte distance past `insns` and the 80-byte `insn_map_x86` layout, the crashing read is `insns[15265].is64bit`. The staged `patch.diff` does not touch this path, but local fix commit `85d1bc7bc406c37e067e10587e6c8f38dc154ee4` changes `is64Bit()` to call `find_insn(id)` before reading `insns[i].is64bit`.

source.description: First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled EVEX state on the crashing path. This accepted EVEX block both classifies the prefix as EVEX and stores the four attacker-controlled EVEX bytes for the later opcode, attribute-mask, and W-bit compensation decisions.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 7-byte blob `00 62 f1 fd 20 15 20`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` computes `i = Data[0] % 33 = 0`, opens `platforms[0] = { CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32 }`, and passes bytes `62 f1 fd 20 15 20` into `cs_disasm()` as the only X86 instruction stream.
source.note: For this witness, the EVEX predicate at lines 585-586 succeeds in `MODE_32BIT` because `byte1 = 0xf1` has high bits `11`, `(~byte1 & 0xc) == 0xc`, and `byte2 = 0xfd` has bit 2 set. The same accepted block then persists `vectorExtensionPrefix[0..3] = { 0x62, 0xf1, 0xfd, 0x20 }`.

sink.description: Crashing read. `is64Bit()` treats the internal decode-table result as a direct index into the public global `insns[]` table and reads past that array.
sink.note: ASan reports this 1-byte read 83,684 bytes to the right of global `insns` (size 1,137,520) in `arch/X86/X86Mapping.c:946`. With 80-byte `insn_map_x86` entries and the `is64bit` field at offset 4, that address is exactly `insns[15265].is64bit`, 1,046 elements beyond the 14,219-entry table.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The decoder passes an internal X86 `InstrUID` into `is64Bit()`, but the vulnerable implementation indexes the separate public `insns[]` mapping table with that UID instead of translating it to a valid mapping-table position first.
root_cause.note: Local fix commit `85d1bc7bc406c37e067e10587e6c8f38dc154ee4` replaces this direct index with `unsigned int i = find_insn(id); if (i != -1) return insns[i].is64bit;`, matching the sparse sorted-ID layout of `insns[]`.

parser_admitted.description: The selector byte `0x00` yields `i = 0`, so the harness opens `CS_ARCH_X86` with `CS_MODE_32`. The saved ASan stack through `is64Bit -> getID -> decodeInstruction` confirms that this X86 decoder path is the one actually reached.

coarse_trace.summary: The 7-byte witness selects the X86 32-bit backend and passes bytes `62 f1 fd 20 15 20` into `cs_disasm()` as the only instruction stream.

The decoder accepts the first four instruction bytes as EVEX, stores them in `vectorExtensionPrefix[]`, consumes opcode `0x15`, and derives the EVEX attribute state used by the later W-bit compensation logic.
The first lookup path requires a ModR/M extension, so `readModRM()` consumes byte `0x20` into `insn->modRM` and leaves it latched for reuse.

Because the instruction is in 32-bit mode but the EVEX W bit is set, `getID()` performs a second lookup with `ATTR_REXW`, obtains the internal UID later seen as `15265`, and `is64Bit()` misuses that UID as a direct `insns[]` index.

fine_trace.note: The accepted EVEX block turns the attacker bytes `62 f1 fd 20` into persistent decoder state: `vectorExtensionType = TYPE_EVEX` and `vectorExtensionPrefix[0..3] = { 0x62, 0xf1, 0xfd, 0x20 }`. Those stored bytes later supply the `mm = VEX_LOB_0F`, `pp = VEX_PREFIX_66`, `W = 1`, and `L = 1` bits used by the crashing path.
Using `mmFromEVEX2of4(insn->vectorExtensionPrefix[1]) == VEX_LOB_0F`, the decoder selects the 0F two-byte opcode map and consumes opcode byte `0x15` into `insn->opcode`.
The stored EVEX bytes produce the base decode attributes for this instruction: `ATTR_EVEX | ATTR_OPSIZE | ATTR_EVEXL`. Because the harness chose `CS_MODE_32`, no `ATTR_64BIT` bit is added here.

During the first `getIDWithAttrMask(&instructionID, insn, attrMask)` lookup, `modRMRequired(...)` is true for opcode `0x15` in this EVEX context, so `readModRM()` consumes the next instruction byte `0x20` into `insn->modRM` and latches it for later reuse.

Because the instruction is not in 64-bit mode and `wFromEVEX3of4(insn->vectorExtensionPrefix[2])` is 1 for byte `0xfd`, `getID()` performs a second lookup with `ATTR_REXW` added. That helper reuses the already stored opcode `0x15` and `insn->modRM = 0x20`; the later ASan offset arithmetic shows that the resulting internal UID passed into `is64Bit()` is `15265`.

The internal UID from step 5 is used as the direct subscript into the public `insns[]` mapping table. For this witness the UID is `15265`, but `insns[]` contains only 14,219 `insn_map_x86` elements, so `is64Bit()` reads one byte from 83,684 bytes past the end of that global array and ASan reports the global-buffer-overflow.

format.name: Exact 7-byte fuzz_disasmnext witness
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 7-byte blob `00 62 f1 fd 20 15 20`. Byte 0 must remain `0x00` so `Data[0] % 33 == 0` selects `platforms[0] = { CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32 }` in this checkout. Bytes 1..6 must remain `62 f1 fd 20 15 20`, because the saved source-grounded chain depends on that exact EVEX block being accepted in 32-bit mode, on `0xf1` selecting the `VEX_LOB_0F` opcode map, on `0xfd` contributing both `pp = VEX_PREFIX_66` and `W = 1`, and on the next byte `0x20` being loaded as the ModR/M byte reused by the second `getIDWithAttrMask(..., ATTR_REXW)` lookup. The available staged artifacts do not justify generalizing this witness into a wider EVEX byte class or a numeric range of internal IDs.
